summary: Migrate a Nuxt2/Vue2 app with Vuex, filters, plugins, middleware, serverMiddleware, asyncData/fetch, and dynamic routes to Nuxt3/Vue3.
solution_steps: Create Nuxt3 config using defineNuxtConfig. Remove target. Move env values to runtimeConfig/public. Revisit modules/buildModules compatibility.
Move Express serverMiddleware endpoints into Nitro server routes under server/api.
Replace Nuxt2 plugin injection with defineNuxtPlugin and nuxtApp.provide.
Replace Vue2 filters with helper functions or composables and update templates accordingly.
Rename dynamic route pages/products/_id.vue to pages/products/[id].vue.
Replace asyncData and legacy fetch with useAsyncData/useFetch in script setup or Nuxt3-compatible setup code.
Replace Vuex usage with Pinia or Nuxt useState for cart/auth state.
Migrate route middleware to defineNuxtRouteMiddleware and update redirect logic using navigateTo.
Check client-only plugin behavior and browser globals under Nuxt3 plugin conventions.
pitfalls: Vue filters are removed in Vue3, so templates using `| currency` or `| titleCase` will break.
Nuxt2 dynamic routes use `_id.vue`; Nuxt3 uses `[id].vue`.
Nuxt2 serverMiddleware with Express/CommonJS does not directly map to Nuxt3 Nitro route handlers.
Nuxt2 context fields like app/env/redirect/error differ from Nuxt3 composables and utilities.
Vuex is not the default Nuxt3 state solution; blindly keeping Vuex increases migration complexity.
Client-only plugins must guard browser globals and use Nuxt3 plugin mode/naming conventions.
